Anthropic's compute commitments have reached $517 billion covering 14.8 gigawatts of capacity through the 11 months ending August 2026. The figure, revealed in regulatory filings reported by The Information, nearly triples prior estimates of roughly $180 billion through 2029—and arrives the same weekend CEO Dario Amodei published his essay urging the industry to slow down.

The commitment breaks down across major partners: Amazon and Alphabet account for approximately 11 gigawatts and more than $300 billion combined. Microsoft contributes over $30 billion at around 1 gigawatt. SpaceX's Colossus cluster represents about $45 billion, while AMD supplies a 2 gigawatt MI450 deal. The scale represents the largest infrastructure bet in artificial intelligence history.

## The Rum Group Structure

The most striking detail lies in the structure. Anthropic is the unnamed customer in Rum Group's $13.7 billion six-year agreement at Maysville, Georgia, structured in three tranches of roughly $4.57 billion each. The deal includes a penny warrant for up to 50.8 million shares worth approximately $364 million. Notably, Rum Group has not secured financing—and Anthropic's obligations are not contingent on it.

This is the kind of term only a company confident of its IPO timeline signs. Anthropic is on the hook regardless of whether the supplier can finance the buildout. The commitment is real, the timeline aggressive, and the confidence visible.

## Profitability and IPO Trajectory

The compute disclosures arrive alongside news of approaching profitability for a second consecutive quarter. Reports indicate IPO discussions at valuations up to $100 billion raised with a potential $2 trillion valuation—would make Anthropic the largest listing in technology history.

The duality is striking: Amodei publicly calls for pacing capability development while the company locks in half a trillion dollars of future compute. But the two positions reconcile when read carefully. The essay advocates pacing capability, not deployment. Fourteen point eight gigawatts is deployment.

The $517 billion number is commitments rather than spend—most lands after 2028, and the Rum Group site does not exist yet. But the figure signals intent. As the AI infrastructure race accelerates, Anthropic is betting that whoever controls compute controls the future.
